theory.intro: A distance–time graph can curve as well as run straight. A straight part means a constant speed; a curved part means the speed is changing. These speed interpretations assume motion along a straight path. Direction statements use distance measured from a fixed reference point, such as home; cumulative distance travelled cannot decrease.
facts: When distance is measured from a fixed reference point, a rising graph means moving **away** from that point; a falling graph means moving **back towards** it. Cumulative distance travelled can rise or remain unchanged, but cannot fall.

A horizontal **interval** means the object is **stopped throughout that interval**, assuming motion along a straight path. A curve with a horizontal tangent at just one instant does not establish a stopped interval.
steps: Check whether the segment rises, falls, or is flat.
Check whether the segment is straight or curved.
If it is curved, check whether it is getting steeper or flatter to describe speeding up or slowing down.

foundation.solution_text:
The curve rises, so Farid is moving away from home.
The curve gets steeper as time passes, and a curve that gets steeper shows the object speeding up, so Farid is speeding up as he moves away from home.

The curve rises, so Priti is moving away from camp.
The curve gets flatter (less steep) as time passes, and a curve that gets flatter shows the object slowing down, so Priti is slowing down as she moves away from camp.

The curve falls, so Cole is moving back towards the start.
The curve gets steeper as time passes, and a curve that gets steeper shows the object speeding up, so Cole is speeding up as he returns to the start.

The curve falls, so Nadia is moving back towards the jetty.
The curve gets flatter (less steep) as time passes, and a curve that gets flatter shows the object slowing down, so Nadia is slowing down as she returns to the jetty.

Ivy's distance from home increases at an increasing rate.
The curve rises and gets steeper, so she moves away from home and speeds up.

development.solution_text:
Stage 1 (the first straight part): the line is straight, so Priti walks at a constant speed to the base of the hill.
Stage 2 (the first curved part): the curve rises but gets flatter, so Priti slows down as she climbs the hill.
Stage 3 (the flat part): the line is horizontal, so Priti is stopped, resting at the top.
Stage 4 (the last curved part): the curve falls and gets steeper, so Priti speeds up as she walks back down towards the start.

Stage 1 (first curved part): the curve rises and gets steeper, so Cole speeds up as he leaves the clubhouse.
Stage 2 (straight part): the line is straight, so Cole rides at a steady pace.
Stage 3 (next curved part): the curve rises but gets flatter, so Cole slows down for the bend.
Stage 4 (last curved part): the curve rises and gets steeper again, so Cole speeds up again after the bend.

Zoe's distance from the start decreases at a decreasing rate.
The curve falls, so the gradient is negative.
The curve gets flatter, so Zoe slows down as she moves towards the start.

During the straight part, Freya walks at a constant speed.
During the curved part, the graph keeps rising but gets flatter, so Freya slows down.
The curve is horizontal at its endpoint, showing zero speed at that instant; there is no horizontal interval showing a period of rest.

The curve becomes steeper as time increases.
Steepness on a distance–time graph shows how fast the distance is changing, so a curve becoming steeper means the distance is changing faster and faster.
This means Sami is speeding up, not slowing down.

The curve falls steeply at first and then gets flatter as time increases.
A falling curve that gets flatter is changing distance more and more slowly, so Jonas is slowing down as he gets closer to home.

mastery.solution_text:
From the start, the curve rises but gets flatter, so Mateo is moving away from the trailhead and slowing down as he climbs.
After the top, the curve falls and gets steeper, so Mateo is moving back towards the trailhead, speeding up as he heads downhill.

Stage A: distance increases, the gradient is positive, and the hiker speeds up as the curve gets steeper.
Stage B: distance increases, the gradient is positive and constant, and the hiker travels at a constant speed.
Stage C: distance increases, the gradient is positive, and the hiker slows down as the curve gets flatter.
Stage D: distance stays the same, the gradient is zero, and the hiker is stopped throughout this horizontal interval.
Stage E: distance decreases, the gradient is negative, and the hiker speeds up towards Camp A as the curve gets steeper.

Stage A: the curve falls and gets steeper, so Rosa moves towards home and speeds up.
Stage B: the line falls at a constant steepness, so Rosa moves towards home at a constant speed.
Stage C: the curve falls and gets flatter, so Rosa moves towards home and slows down.
Stage D: the line is horizontal, so Rosa is stopped throughout this interval.
Stage E: the curve rises and gets steeper, so Rosa moves away from home and speeds up.
